page: Microsoft Azure E48bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The instance provisions 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores using simultaneous multithreading, supported by 48 MB of L3 cache. It provides 384 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. In addition to compute and memory, the configuration bundles 1,933 GB of local solid-state storage.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the upper quartile for parallel compute and memory-dependent operations. The server achieved a multi-core Geekbench score of 15,896.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 50,758.8. PassMark database operations registered at 23,567.62, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 221.85 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25 percent. The x86_64 platform also features hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions, contributing to a strong PassMark CPU encryption score of 43,881.16.

Single-core compute figures reflect standard mid-tier throughput, with a single-core Geekbench score of 1,689.0 and a stress-ng single-core result of 1,900.08. Lacking dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, the system is less suited for heavy machine learning text generation, recording 2.33 tokens per second on 70B parameter models. However, the presence of 1,933 GB of local SSD storage provides significant fast scratch disk capacity without requiring external disk attachments for temporary structures.

Microsoft Azure E48bds_v5 is structured for enterprise database engines, in-memory cache stores, software compilation systems, and large-scale data extraction and transformation pipelines that depend on high RAM capacity alongside local disk space.
description: Microsoft Azure E48bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The configuration allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores, 384 GB of RAM, and 1,933 GB of local SSD storage. Delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the system achieves top-quartile results in multi-core metrics, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,896.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 50,758.8. It also demonstrates high multi-threaded decompression throughput and strong database operational scores. While single-thread execution remains in the median range and the lack of discrete GPUs limits large-model generative AI tasks, the high resource density and bundled local storage provide significant utility for memory-heavy setups. This instance is suited for enterprise relational databases, in-memory caching systems, extensive software compilation workflows, and large-scale data analytics pipelines.
